start_here: Say to your AI: "Label the two sampled frames of my video with the open_clip model some/clip, using my shot vocabulary of size (wide, close) and colour (red, blue)."

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Pour the two example settings rows into your own list:settings (see pour), or write your own row record:setting:benchmark-small-local-models~person~<you> whose settings hold {"commands":{"label_frames_with_image_text_model":{...your defaults}}}.
2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads this tool's row with tools:list {tool: "tool:label-video-frames-with-small-local-models"} and gets its run command.

3. Your AI writes the request as a JSON file (request.json), adds settings_record from your settings row if you keep one, and runs python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/label_frames_with_image_text_model.py request.json on your computer.
4. It reads the last line the script prints: {"result": ...} or {"error": "what to change"} (exit code 2), then tells you the result in plain words.

5. Other steps of this tool: label_frames_with_vision_decider (one lettered question per field), label_frames_with_vision_language_model (one JSON answer per frame) and rank_free_text_places; write_to keeps each answer in a file you can hand to tool:score-small-model-labels-against-my-labels.

worked_examples.title: Two frames labelled for size and colour by an image-text model
worked_examples.ask: Label these two frames from my video with my size and colour words.
worked_examples.given: From tools/benchmark-small-local-models/test/test_benchmark.py (Labels.test_image_text_model_ranks_each_value_bare_and_defined), run with the test's stand-in model. After tools:list, the AI writes request.json = {"shots":[{"frame":"a.png","reference":{"place":"red room"},"w":1920,"h":1080},{"frame":"b.png","reference":{"place":"blue sky"},"w":1080,"h":1920}],"vocabulary":{"size":{"wide":"a wide shot of the whole place","close":"a close shot of a face"},"colour":{"red":"a red frame","blue":"a blue frame"}},"model":"some/clip","tag":"clip","device":"cpu"} (a.png is a picture of a wide red room, b.png of a close blue one) and runs: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/label_frames_with_image_text_model.py request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result":{"meta":{"model":"some/clip","tag":"clip","n":2,"mps_GB":null,...},"rows":[{"i":0,"size|bare":["wide","close"],"size|bare|all":[0.71416,0.02127],"size|defined":["wide","close"],"colour|bare":["red","blue"],"colour|defined":["red","blue"],...},{"i":1,"size|bare":["close","wide"],"colour|bare":["blue","red"],"colour|defined":["blue","red"],...}]}}: each value is ranked best first, once by its bare word and once by its plain definition, one row per frame, with load seconds, time per image and memory in meta.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
